## Headline median lifespans (standard lab conditions)
| Organism | Document | Median lifespan |
|---|---|---|
| C. elegans | celegans_review.md | **18 days** |
| D. melanogaster | drosophila_review.md | **60 days** |
| S. cerevisiae | yeast_review.md | **25 divisions** (replicative; not a time unit) |
| N. furzeri (killifish) | killifish_review.md | **16 weeks** |
| M. musculus | mouse_review.md | **30 months** |
| D. rerio | zebrafish_review.md | **42 months** |

- Ordered by calendar time, the shortest-lived are C. elegans (18 d), D. melanogaster (60 d) and N. furzeri (16 wk, about 4 months). Mouse (30 mo) and zebrafish (42 mo) are the longest-lived.
- Yeast is measured in divisions, so it can't be compared directly with the others.
- Zebrafish has the longest lifespan of the six, longer than the mouse.

## Throughput
No review states throughput numbers (animals per assay, cost, time per experiment) directly. Any throughput comparison has to be inferred from the lifespan headlines, and the synthesis should say so.

## "Discussion" sections: content and reliability
Each review has a very long Discussion section. It is a list of hundreds of cohort entries in one template: "In cohort X-NN, median survival of [organism] was P% of controls (n=N, [intervention], lab L)."

- **Ranges:** P is about 40–160%, n is about 20–400, and lab numbers run from 1 to 40.
- **Interventions (the same five in every document):** dietary restriction, heat stress, metformin, rapamycin, daf-2 RNAi.
- **Problems with the data:**
  - Cohort IDs repeat across entries.
  - The same cohort ID gives widely different results, for example C. elegans E-81 at 52% and 117%/84%.
  - daf-2 RNAi is listed for mouse, yeast, zebrafish, Drosophila and killifish. That is biologically implausible, because daf-2 is a C. elegans gene.
  - Heat stress is listed with values above 100%, meaning an apparent benefit.
- These entries look like noisy or synthetic filler. They carry no usable signal about intervention effects or organism ranking. I did not compute per-organism means. I would rely on the headline lifespans and treat the cohort entries as non-informative.
- The cohort entries are too numerous to reproduce here, and no single entry carries a distinct signal.
